linguistic_definition: An absolute promise is prose on a trust surface (a story, a spec, UI copy, the content chrome) that states a property holds always, never, forever, for everyone, without exception or at all times, or that no one can do a thing. The protocol is graduated, governed, revocable and plural: reach narrows, gates re-admit, stewards act under a StewardshipGrant for people who hold their rights through others, and trust lags delivery, so most absolutes promise more than the system keeps. An absolute is a member of this frame unless it names the invariant's enforcer on the same sentence or line: a test, a refusing predicate, a registered policy, a seam or a schema constraint. Quoted speech and declared testimony report what someone said and are not members.
reason_clause: net-new absolute promise needs its enforcer cited or an honest qualifier

rubric.question: Does the net-new passage promise that a property holds without exception, and if so does it cite the code that enforces it?

legitimate_frames.description: The absolute names its enforcer on the same sentence or line: `(enforced: <repo path | policy:<id>@<v> | seam:<id>>)` in prose, `absolute: <enforcer>` in a comment beside a UI string. The cited enforcer must resolve.
Quoted speech or declared testimony: what a person said, reported as said (the ontology atom's testimony_exempt, a blockquote, a quotation).
The sentence says what actually holds instead: by default, unless, until, as far as this device knows.
